title: Mavs' Caleb Martin Hasn't Played Modern Warfare 4 Yet
htmlContent:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has taken over gaming conversations across the country, and NBA locker rooms are no exception. Dallas Mavericks wing Caleb Martin says the new game has been a hot topic among his teammates, but he hasn't had a chance to jump in yet.

When asked if he had played the latest installment of the blockbuster franchise, Martin kept it honest.

"No, I haven't got to. I've been hearing about it in the locker room, so I haven't got a chance to play yet. But I ain't had too much time outside this, so I'm hoping to get on that pretty soon."

The Locker Room Buzz

Martin's answer says a lot about how big a new Call of Duty release is, even inside an NBA facility. Video games have long been part of locker room culture, giving players a way to unwind, compete and bond away from the court. On team flights, in hotel rooms and at home between games, consoles often travel right along with the roster.

Call of Duty in particular has a deep following among professional athletes. Its fast-paced multiplayer modes feed the same competitive drive that pushes players during games, and trash talk over a headset can be just as intense as anything said on the hardwood.

For Martin, the buzz has been loud enough that he knows exactly what he is missing. His teammates have clearly been talking about it, and it sounds like he is ready to join the conversation once his schedule opens up.

What Modern Warfare 4 Brings

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launched on October 23, 2026, with Infinity Ward returning to lead development. The game is available on PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S and Nintendo Switch 2, and it skips last-generation consoles.

The campaign centers on a North Korean invasion of the Korean Peninsula, with missions that also move through New York, Paris and Mumbai. Players can expect trench warfare in Korea, close-quarters fights in New York, chases through Paris and night raids in Mumbai.

Multiplayer focuses on grounded, precise combat with fluid movement and more player control. The game also brings back DMZ, where players work as off-the-books operatives behind enemy lines and make tough choices about which objectives to chase and when to get out.

With that much content, it is no surprise the game has become a regular topic in the Mavericks' locker room.

Busy Start to the Season

Martin's comment that he hasn't "had too much time outside this" reflects the grind of an NBA season. Between practices, film sessions, travel, treatment and games, players have little free time, especially early in the year when teams are still building chemistry and routines.

Martin has also been working through a thumb injury that cost him a game in late October. He returned to play in the Mavericks' 120-96 win over the Oklahoma City Thunder on October 28, scoring 10 points in 14 minutes. Early in November, he was expected to move into the starting lineup, adding even more responsibility to his plate.

With that kind of schedule, gaming naturally takes a back seat. Martin's focus right now is on getting healthy, earning minutes and helping Dallas win.

More Than Just a Game

Still, moments like this offer fans a glimpse of the person behind the jersey. Athletes are often seen only through stats and highlights, but questions about video games, music or hobbies show a more relatable side.

Martin's answer is something many working fans can understand. A big new game drops, friends are already playing, and life keeps getting in the way. Plenty of people have experienced that same struggle of wanting to play but not having the time.

Gaming has also become a growing part of the NBA world. Many players stream, invest in esports organizations or partner with gaming brands. Video games give athletes a way to connect with younger fans who spend as much time online as they do watching basketball.

Hoping to Log On Soon

Martin made it clear he plans to join his teammates in Modern Warfare 4 "pretty soon." Once he does, he may have some catching up to do, since others in the locker room have already been putting in the hours.

That could make for some fun competition. If Martin brings the same energy and toughness to Call of Duty that he brings to the court, his teammates may not have the upper hand for long. Locker room bragging rights can be a big deal, and a few late-night matches on the road could become another way for this group to build chemistry away from the floor.

For now, though, the Mavericks wing is locked in on basketball. Modern Warfare 4 will have to wait until he finds a little more time away from the gym.
excerpt: Dallas Mavericks wing Caleb Martin says Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has been a hot topic in the locker room, but the busy NBA schedule has kept him from jumping in — though he's hoping to find time soon.
